verdict.rationale: Honcho's docs say the core is open source and that you can run the whole thing yourself on your own infrastructure. The CLI's `honcho start` brings up the full stack (API, deriver, Postgres, Redis) via Docker, and the MCP server can also run locally instead of the hosted endpoint. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of self-hosted deployments, in-depth production self-hosting docs (configuration, scaling, upgrades).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: The core is open source at github.com/plastic-labs/honcho, so you can run the whole thing yourself and keep your data on your own infrastructure.
honcho start runs API, deriver, Postgres, and Redis via Docker.
Skip `mcp.honcho.dev` and run the MCP server locally over stdio, Streamable HTTP, or Docker.
Honcho is an open-source memory layer for AI agents, built by Plastic Labs.
